description.narrative: In 2021 Inter-Governmental Authority on Development (IGAD) developed and endorsed regional guidelines on right based bilateral labour agreements at the IGAD Experts Validation Workshop on July 7th 2021.The guideline was endorsed by experts from Ministries of Labour and Employment and social partners of IGAD member states after series of virtual and face to face consultation and validation by senior experts of all IGAD member states. The guidelines draw on practical experiences of IGAD member states through a review of more than 40 existing bilateral labour agreements (BLAs) signed by IGAD member states with major countries of destination in the Middle East and extensive consultation with all key stakeholders involved in the drafting, negotiation and implementation of BLAs in all IGAD member states. This guidelines includes mutually agreed measures and solutions for crisis and emergency management, like the situation of COVID 19, based on the principle of equality of treatment of migrant workers and national workers. The agreed measures, if applied to new and revised BLAs, would ensure that these instruments are in line with international standards. Furthermore, the guidelines includes specific guidance on the development of monitoring and review mechanisms in the BLA process. The lessons learned and good practices documented in the background report and the guidelines will serve as reference for developing effective monitoring and evaluation framework for BLAs at national level. With support from the European Union, the ILO funded a background study on bilateral labour agreements (BLAs) in the Inter-Governmental Authority on Development (IGAD) region, developed the IGAD regional guidelines on rights based BLAs, and a policy brief on BLAs. The background report reviewed more than 40 existing bilateral labour agreements (BLAs) signed by IGAD member states with major countries of destination in the Middle East and extensive consultation with all key stakeholders involved in the drafting, negotiation and implementation of BLAs in all IGAD member states. The ILO also convened four virtual and face to face consultations and validation workshops (December 2020 and June-July 2021) to discuss the draft guidelines document and obtain technical endorsement of the document by Ministries of Labour and social partners, which will culminate in the organization of the IGAD ministerial conference planned for October 2021 which among other things is expected to endorse the regional guidelines. The final version of the Guidelines to be endorsed by the Ministers of Labour and Employment of IGAD member states incorporates changes based on the ILO comments in line with the international standards. In the next biennium, ILO will continue to provide support to developing effective monitoring and evaluation framework for BLAs at national level.

Output 1.1. Increased institutional capacity of employer and business membership organizations (EBMOs)

description.narrative: In December 2019, the Confederation of the Intergovernmental Authority on Development Employers (CIE), a regional umbrella of employers' organization in the IGAD region, was established to complement the Horn of Africa Confederation of Trade Unions (HACTU), a regional umbrella of trade unions organizations. Employers Organizations from Djibouti, Ethiopia, South Sudan, Sudan and Uganda signed the By-Laws during the launching of the CIE in Nairobi Kenya on 11 December 2019 in the presence of the HACTU, the Intergovernmental Authority on Development (IGAD) and ILO Representatives. In January 2020, CIE nominated its first President. CIE held its first General Assembly in February 2021, officially complementing the governance issues required for the organizations full functioning. Specifically, CEI elected 3 vice presidents and 3 board members, nominated a secretary general, and also recruited a public relations and auditor to serve the CIE secretariat. The CIE also launched a dedicated web site so members have ease of access to latest information impacting the Horn of Africa business community and its policy priorities. In July 2021, following the Annual General Meetings of CIE and HACTU held concurrently at the same venue in Uganda, CIE and HACTU signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) on how they would work together with the IGAD Secretariat. The MoU serves as the basis for CIE's strategic plan, outlining the main axes for operation of CIE with its partners. This development is an important progress in the establishment of a functional regional tripartism and social dialogue for the mainstreaming of decent work issues in the implementation of the protocol on free movement of persons and transhumance in the IGAD region. CIE fills a void for employer organizations in member countries to cooperate and address issues that go beyond national boundaries such as labour movement and trade, issues national employer organizations on their own would not be able to address. From 2019 to 2021 with support from the European Union, the ILO supported three sensitization and capacity building workshops for the social partners in the IGAD region to enhance the mainstreaming of decent work issues at the regional level. The initiative for the creation of the CIE was taken by the employer's organizations during the Social Partners Sensitization workshop on the draft IGAD protocol on Free Movement held in May 2019. In December 2019, the ILO Free movement of Persons and Transhumance project supported the establishment of the CIE by organizing a tripartite workshop in Nairobi Kenya on ILS related to labour migration. The ILO facilitated a series of consultation and coordination initiatives between the CIE and HACTU which culminated to the organization of two concurrent stocktaking workshops and Annual General Meetings at the same venue in July 2021, after which CIE and HACTU held a joint session to deliberate on their key areas of collaboration.
